confidence: Kumon's observed rice in nominal monme, 1695-1711, half again Kyoho's. Priced at the Genroku silver of 1695-1705 (64%, 2.40 g a monme); the Hoei silvers of 1706-1711 were baser, but rice in them stood where it had under Genroku. The ryo and mon rates are 1700's, and BORROWED for 1706-1711, which no source in hand rates. The wage is borrowed.

monme.note: Genroku silver (1695-1705), 2.40 g pure; market rates of 1700 (47-48 monme a ryo, 3.71 kanmon a ryo), borrowed for 1706-1711

bu.note: A quarter of a ryo (the gold count: 4 bu a ryo)

shu.note: A sixteenth of a ryo (16 shu a ryo)

rice.label: historical
rice.note: 0.452 monme a kg, Kumon's observed 1695-1711 (17 years)

wage.note: BORROWED: none found for these years; the reference day (0.907 monme) chained by Kumon's farm-servant year, 92.3 monme in 1695-1711 and 113.9 in 1745-1754, in grams of silver
